correctness.rationale: A direct M-matrix resolvent proof shows the Perron growth boundary r_c=aN/H. Exact positive polynomial denominator and derivative numerator a²(a+q)+2(a+q)(2a-q)d+(5a-3q)d² give a strict monotone regime and unique interior maximum precisely at q>5a/3. A cooperative quadratic-crowding argument proves extinction when the Perron root is nonpositive and a unique globally attracting positive equilibrium when positive, including the two equality boundaries. The two-patch threshold is monotone. The attached standard-library checker reconstructs determinant, cofactor and derivative identities; finite tests are supplementary, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The headwater reproduction versus downstream-drift tradeoff is a natural idealization of the drift paradox. A complete exact drift-to-mortality boundary makes intermediate diffusion uniquely harmful, but sufficient diffusion rescues the source patch; an explicit strict rational witness demonstrates the reversal and proves three patches minimal in this family. This is a nontrivial qualitative phase classification of nonlinear population persistence, not an arbitrary sampled parameter case or generic numerical gain. It provides a reusable benchmark for heterogeneous stream networks; no field-calibrated conservation implication is claimed.
